title: Bernstorff (German Embassy Washington), second code text on the State Department cable of 11 Jan 1917 (groups 147-576), unread
correspondents: Count Johann Heinrich von Bernstorff → Auswärtiges Amt, Berlin (via Secretary Lansing and Amembassy Berlin)
folio_note: Roll 166 frames 0785-0786 (sheets 1 and 2; 0786 is not reversed): 577 groups in all (505 four-figure, 67 five-figure, 4 three-figure, 1 six-figure). Groups 0-146 are telegram No. 205; groups 147-576 are a second text in the same code.
status: 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #115; targets/bernstorff1917/): groups 0-146 are Bernstorff's telegram No. 205 of 10 Jan 1917, printed by Bernstorff (1920, pp. 325-326) and in Official German Documents II p. 1017; aligning them gave 82 groups of a two-part four-figure code with prefix figures (not 13040; probably 0075 [?]). Written up. The memorandum on frames 0769-0775 is not the plaintext. This entry is now the second text, 430 groups in the same code, unread; catalogue 635 (5 Dec 1916) is the sibling to try.
why: A German Embassy code telegram of the last weeks before unrestricted U-boat warfare, with a near-certain crib; a test of the 13040/0075 codes on known text.

title: German Minister at Lima (Perl) ↔ German legations Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Mexico: copies of cipher telegrams obtained by the US Legation Lima
correspondents: German Legation Lima (Minister Perl; later Weyers) ↔ German legations in Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Mexico
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Central Decimal File 1910-29, 862.20223 (German military activities in Peru), sub-nos. 4-99
folio_note: The 862.20223 file is scanned: M336 roll 64 (RG 64 copy, item naId 574876562), frames c. 0048-0207 and later (found 27 Oct 2026 in the NARA bulk sweep, slice J). It holds the US Legation's relays of the German code telegrams (5-figure groups), a letter code between Quito and Lima (f.0104), the Department's re-sends 'For Bell from Harrison' (f.0049-0054, 0069, 0103, 0129-0132, 0204), London's replies (f.0101 'Second undecipherable ... Fourth undecipherable'; f.0207 a verbatim English text), Lima's despatch of 6 June 1917 (f.0070-0072) and Handley's of 9 Oct 1917 (f.0205). Purport list: M973 roll 207 frames 1008-1014.
status: Partially read at the time: London (Bell / Gunther, i.e. Room 40 via the US Embassy) cabled back the 'substance' of most batches; Lima 85 (9 Oct 1917) reports some messages could not be deciphered. Verbatim decodes not listed. Not on DECODE; not in the repo.
why: German diplomatic traffic along the west coast of South America in 1917, with a contemporary partial reading to check against.

title: Case MS 5017 occult manuscript (17th c.), folio with a characters table and two sample lines 'in cipher'
correspondents: unknown (compiler not identified; not verified to be Robert Ashley)
shelfmark: Newberry Library, Case MS 5017 (digital item case_ms_5017_020_o2, CONTENTdm nby_dig/2714)
folio_note: one page: table of symbols paired with letters, with two sample ciphertexts transcribed in the image alt-text as 'edward; eliet' and 'writ; tsis'
status: Digitised page: 'This Table which standeth here underneth serveth them who are desirous to use a form of Characters to write in that maner that no man shall reade; but by the Table folowing.' The page carries its own key, so the examples are readable. This is a key lead, not an unsolved text; the other pages (case_ms_5017_070_o2 matched 'code') may hold further cipher material and are worth a look. The volume's catalogue record was not matched (Ashley's 1612 'Book of magical charms' is a separate digital record, not shown to be this volume). Not on DECODE; known.py no hit for Case MS 5017.
why: Shows a 17th-century amateur cipher alphabet inside an occult manuscript; useful as a key for any unread characters elsewhere in the volume.

title: Ferdinand and Isabella → De Puebla, Tortosa, 28 Dec 1495, cipher copy in Puebla's Great Roman Numeral code
correspondents: Ferdinand and Isabella → Rodrigo González de Puebla
shelfmark: AGS, Patronato Real, LEG,52, DOC.124
folio_note: PARES description 2207846, 4 images (pp. 1-4, foliation 664-665; old mark T. c. Y. 2). Sample decoded: p. 1 ll. 6-8 and p. 2 ll. 1-6; the rest of the cipher copy not decoded.
status: Identified 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #101; targets/puebla1495/): the cipher copy of the despatch of 28 Dec 1495 whose clear draft Bergenroth abstracted in CSP Spain I no. 113 (no. 114 notices the cipher copy, 'substance exactly the same', with no decipherment); five sending dates on p. 2 match no. 113 and no other item. A sample (p. 1 ll. 6-8) decoded with the extant key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33. Open: the cipher copy beyond the sample, and the groups 883, 1374, 1335, 1813, 852, 868, 1221 and 'xxix' (key images not opened: PARES HTTP 429). No page.
why: Anglo-Spanish diplomacy of 1495 (Perkin Warbeck, the Catherine of Aragon marriage treaty) in a code whose 2400-element key survives.
